international.canonicalTopic: Michael Kremer appointed World Bank Chief Economist
international.headline: Michael Kremer appointed World Bank Chief Economist
facts: Nobel laureate Michael Kremer was appointed World Bank Chief Economist, succeeding Indermit Gill.
Kremer was to assume office on 1 October 2026, ahead of the World Bank–IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok.
He is a University of Chicago professor and jointly received the 2019 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for research on an experimental approach to alleviating global poverty.
The World Bank President named in the notes is Ajay Banga; the institution is headquartered in Washington, D.C.
international.summary: Michael Kremer’s appointment brings an economist known for experimental research on poverty alleviation to the World Bank Chief Economist position.
international.staticLink: The World Bank’s major institutions include the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Kremer succeeded Indermit Gill and was scheduled to take office on 1 October 2026.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the value of evidence-based and experimental approaches in development policy and poverty reduction.

national.canonicalTopic: Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026
national.headline: Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 takes effect on October 1
facts: The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 came into force on 2026-10-01, as fixed by the Central Government through a Gazette notification.
The Bill passed both Houses of Parliament and received President Droupadi Murmu’s assent in August 2026.

For registration delayed by more than one year but less than two years, permission from a Judicial Magistrate and the prescribed fee are required; delays exceeding two years require a special order from a First-Class Magistrate.
The amendment strengthens provisions to prevent delays in registration. The original law is the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.
The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India is the national implementing authority; the nodal ministry is the Ministry of Home Affairs.
national.summary: The 2026 amendment to the Registration of Births and Deaths Act came into force on October 1, introducing specified magistrate permissions and orders for delayed registration.
national.staticLink: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, as amended in 2026.
national.prelimsTakeaway: A delay of more than one year but less than two years requires Judicial Magistrate permission; a delay exceeding two years requires a First-Class Magistrate’s special order.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how timely civil registration supports public administration, legal identity and reliable demographic data.

sources.title: Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act–2026 to Come into Force from October 1

national.notes:
# 1. What happened
- **What:** The **Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026** came into force on **October 1, 2026**.
- **When:** Effective date fixed by the **Central Government** through a **Gazette notification**.
# 2. Rules for delayed registration
| Delay | Requirement |
|---|---|
| More than **1 year** but less than **2 years** | Permission from a **Judicial Magistrate** and the **prescribed fee** |
| Exceeding **2 years** | Special order from a **First-Class Magistrate** |
- **Objective:** Strengthening provisions to prevent delays in registration.
- ⚠ **Trap:** A delay of more than **1 year** but less than **2 years** requires **Judicial Magistrate** permission; a delay exceeding **2 years** requires a **First-Class Magistrate’s** special order.
# 3. Legislative and implementation framework
- **Parliamentary passage:** Bill passed both Houses of **Parliament**; received assent from **President Droupadi Murmu** in **August 2026**.
- **Original law:** **Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969**.
- **Implementing authority:** **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India**.
- **Nodal ministry:** **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
- **Andhra Pradesh link:** No direct **Andhra Pradesh**-specific link established.
# 4. Also note
- The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 came into force on 2026-10-01, as fixed by the Central Government through a Gazette notification.
> Exam angle: Test the amendment’s commencement date, nodal ministry and magistrate-authorisation requirements for different periods of delayed registration.
